title: Identifying Best Practices for Improving the Evaluation and Management of Stroke in Rural Lower-Resourced Settings: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
authors: American Heart Association Emergency Neurovascular Care and Telestroke Committee of the Stroke Council; Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing; and Council on Cardiovascular Radiology and Intervention
summary: This AHA scientific statement addresses acute stroke care in rural and lower-resourced settings, where many patients initially present to community EDs without stroke-center resources. It recommends system-level strategies including written stroke protocols, telestroke access, rapid imaging transfer, hub-and-spoke mentorship, standardized transfer pathways, quality-improvement participation, and efforts to shorten door-in-door-out time for thrombectomy candidates. It also supports geographically efficient expansion of Acute Stroke Ready Hospital and Primary Stroke Center capability.
findings: The statement identifies remote community EDs as anchors of the rural stroke chain of survival and emphasizes written protocols, simulation, telestroke, and stronger hub relationships.

For transfer-dependent thrombectomy care, it supports rapid vascular imaging, early parallel engagement of tertiary centers, image sharing, established transfer agreements, and door-in-door-out optimization.

Expansion of Acute Stroke Ready Hospital and Primary Stroke Center certification, better EMS/routing infrastructure, data integration, and quality-improvement participation are proposed to reduce rural disparities.
comparator: Existing heterogeneous rural stroke systems and resource availability; the statement itself is not a comparative trial.
population: Patients with suspected or confirmed stroke presenting to rural or lower-resourced US EMS systems, emergency departments, hospitals, and transfer networks.
limitations: This is a systems-of-care scientific statement built largely from observational evidence, quality-improvement data, and expert consensus rather than randomized comparisons of the proposed system interventions. Feasibility depends heavily on local staffing, transport, imaging, telehealth, and regional resources.
intervention: System-level strategies to improve rural acute stroke access and performance, including stroke-center readiness, telestroke, standardized protocols, rapid imaging and transfer, hub mentorship, and quality improvement.
whyItMatters: For community and rural EDs, the practical message is to build stroke capability before the patient arrives: standardized protocols, immediate telestroke access, rapid CTA/image sharing, parallel transfer activation, and explicit relationships with receiving stroke centers. The statement changes systems planning more than bedside drug selection.
evidenceNotes: Historical backfill. PubMed verifies Epub 2024-12-12, PMID 39665145, and DOI 10.1161/STR.0000000000000478; the official AHA summary and open full text were reviewed. A targeted correction/retraction search did not identify a correction or retraction. This is systems-level historical guidance; later 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guidance should govern current disease-specific treatment recommendations.
primaryEndpoint: Critical appraisal and consensus strategies for improving acute stroke evaluation, treatment access, transfer, and quality in rural lower-resourced settings.
guidelineStrength: American Heart Association scientific statement based on critical appraisal and expert consensus; it is not a single uniformly GRADE-rated recommendation set.
